newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Gdansk Refinery to acquire small refiner.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Gdansk Refinery to acquire small refiner.

text.p: Rafineria Gdanska SA said it signed a letter of intent with state-controlled Nafta Polska SA to acquire 75 percent of Rafineria Nafty Jedlicze SA.

The Gdansk refinery said in a statement that the final conditions of the agreement were still being negotiated, but it was likely that 70 percent of Jedlicze's shares would be contributed by Nafta Polska as a capital increase.
"The remaining five percent would be sold (by Nafta Polska)," Gdansk refinery said on Wednesday.

The transaction is a part of the oil sector restructuring under which two production groups would be created around the country's two largest refineries. In February, Poland's largest refiner, Petrochemia Plock SA, took over 75 percent of the small southern Trzebinia refinery.

Under the Nafta Polska plan, the groups would be set for partial privatisation by the end of the year. Nafta said prospective investors were expected to guarantee oil supplies from their own resources.

Petrochemia Plock has capacity to process 12.6 million tonnes of crude oil a year and Rafineria Gdansk produced 2.8 million tonnes last year. Jedlicze has a capacity of 200,000 tonnes and Trzebinia 300,000 tonnes.
